jp: 母[はは]{は/が|wa-topic}台所[だいどころ]{で|de-place}何[なに]{か|ka-indefinite}作[つく]っています。
en: My mother is making something in the kitchen.
why: 何か means an unspecified "something"; 何が/何を would turn the sentence into a question.

jp: 誰[だれ]{か|ka-indefinite}{が|ga-subject}玄関[げんかん]{で|de-place}待[ま]っています。
en: Someone is waiting at the front door.
why: 誰か means an unidentified "someone"; the other particles cannot attach to 誰 here.

jp: 週末[しゅうまつ]、どこ{か|ka-indefinite}{に/へ|ni-destination}行[い]きません{か|ka-question}。
en: Shall we go somewhere this weekend?
why: どこか means "somewhere" without naming the place, and に/へ then marks the destination.

jp: いつ{か|ka-indefinite}、大[おお]きい家[いえ]{に|ni-location}住[す]みたいです。
en: Someday I want to live in a big house.
why: いつか means "some time or other" in the unspecified future; the other particles make no sense after いつ.

jp: 弟[おとうと]{が|ga-subject}何[なに]{か|ka-indefinite}{を|o-object}飲[の]んでいます。
en: My younger brother is drinking something.
why: 何か makes "something" indefinite, and を then marks it as the thing being drunk.

jp: 今朝[けさ]、誰[だれ]{か|ka-indefinite}{に|ni-target}電話[でんわ]{を|o-object}かけました。
why: 誰か is "someone" unnamed; に then marks the person who was called.

jp: 夕飯[ゆうはん]{の|no-possessive}あとで、家族[かぞく]{と|to-with}何[なに]{か|ka-indefinite}ゲーム{を|o-object}しません{か|ka-question}。
en: Shall we play some game with the family after dinner?
why: 何か + noun means "some kind of" (here, some game); the other particles break the phrase.

jp: 部屋[へや]{の|no-possessive}中[なか]{で|de-place}何[なに]{か|ka-indefinite}{が|ga-subject}動[うご]きました。
why: 何か means an unidentified "something"; も would need a negative verb and を/に do not fit 何 here.
